subject: Dance
_width_axis_note: Width in dance varies by the range of styles, choreographic contexts, performance conditions and expressive demands students engage with. A student at minimum width works within one familiar style or context; wider students work across multiple styles, contexts and increasingly self-directed choreographic problems.

AC9ADA8C01.minimum_width: Choreograph a short dance phrase by selecting and sequencing movements using at least one choreographic device; explain how the device communicates an intended idea, perspective or meaning.
AC9ADA8C01.typical_width: Choreograph dance using a range of choreographic devices (transitions, variation, contrast) and structural forms; document and justify choices about how elements of dance and devices communicate intended meaning.
wider: Explore how the same choreographic material communicates differently when produced for different contexts — live performance, music video, VR immersive experience — and evaluate what changes and why

Select movements from improvisation and organise them into structured dance using multiple choreographic devices; document how the selection and structuring process changes what the dance communicates
Choreograph dance that portrays characters or social relationships with empathy — evaluate whether the choreographic choices achieve the intended respectful communication
elaborations: exploring ways to use elements of dance and choreographic devices to portray characters and stories respectfully and empathetically
experimenting with elements of dance and choreographic devices to represent ideas about themes or issues such as social relationships
selecting movements from improvisation and organising for use in a music video or immersive experience
selecting, combining, refining and sequencing movement using choreographic devices such as transitions, variation and contrast, and forms such as binary, ternary and narrative
analysing and evaluating structural choices in their dance by documenting process in journals, blogs, video or audio recordings

AC9ADA8C02.minimum_width: Apply at least one technical or expressive skill (e.g. balance, strength, projection) to communicate mood or intention in a dance; explain how the skill contributes to the communication.
AC9ADA8C02.typical_width: Apply technical and expressive skills across a dance to communicate choreographic intent consistently; respond to feedback to refine technical accuracy and expressive clarity; document decisions.
wider: Use Viewpoints questions to evaluate clarity of movement, projection, focus and musicality in preparation for performance — use video to evaluate and refine spatial placement or articulation
Apply genre- or style-specific techniques to perform in a style distinct from everyday movement — evaluate how technique mastery changes what the dance communicates
Intensify communication of mood or atmosphere by combining multiple technical skills simultaneously — document the challenge of coordinating technical demands with expressive intent
elaborations: applying technical skills such as strength, balance or coordination to intensify communication of mood/atmosphere
responding to feedback to enhance communication of choreographic intent to the audience
using Viewpoints to evaluate clarity of movement, projection, focus and musicality; using video to evaluate and refine

AC9ADA8D01.minimum_width: Develop at least one technical or expressive skill through deliberate practice; describe what improved and how the improvement affects the dance.
AC9ADA8D01.typical_width: Develop technical competence and expressive range through sustained practice across multiple skills; extend movement vocabulary by experimenting with movements from diverse dance styles; respond to feedback to guide practice.
wider: Improvise using movements and techniques from diverse dance styles to extend own movement vocabulary — document what each style adds to the available expressive range
Explore how expressive skills (gesture, facial expression) communicate relationships or emotions and experiment with extending range beyond familiar movement
Investigate how safe dance practice principles apply differently across styles and physical demands — develop a personal safe practice protocol for own dance work
elaborations: developing dance skills and style-specific techniques — improvising using movements and techniques from diverse dance styles to extend movement vocabulary
exploring how expressive skills can be used to communicate ideas — using gesture or facial expression to communicate relationships or emotions
extending technical competence such as control, coordination, accuracy, alignment, balance, flexibility, strength, endurance and articulation in response to feedback

AC9ADA8D02.minimum_width: Reflect on at least one aspect of own dance work using feedback from self, peer or teacher; document one specific change made as a result of the reflection.
AC9ADA8D02.typical_width: Use reflection on own and others' dance works to inform choreographic choices and technical/expressive skill use; document influences and decisions in a journal; evaluate how reflection is changing practice over time.
wider: Document interesting examples of how others use an element of dance or style-specific techniques in a journal — develop a personal archive of influences that informs own choreography and performance
Reflect on how movement vocabulary has extended across a unit — identify specific moments where encountering other dancers' work opened new directions in own practice
Evaluate own performance or choreography against a specific set of criteria — use findings to set targeted goals for future practice
elaborations: reflecting on how they have used or extended their movement vocabulary and considering options for further development
evaluating influences on own performance or choreography — documenting examples of how others use elements of dance or style-specific techniques
reflecting on feedback from peers who have observed a workshop or rehearsal and using ideas to refine dance

AC9ADA8E01.minimum_width: Investigate how at least one dance work, performer or choreographer uses elements of dance or choreographic devices to communicate ideas or meaning; explain the relationship between specific choices and the meaning communicated.
AC9ADA8E01.typical_width: Investigate dance works across cultures, times or places; analyse how elements of dance and choreographic devices are manipulated to communicate ideas; explain how context shapes choreographic choices.
wider: Compare how the same element of dance (e.g. repetition) is used across dances from different genres, cultures or times — analyse what changes and what persists across contexts
Investigate how digital tools and immersive technologies (VR) are influencing choreography and performance — analyse how new technologies create new expressive possibilities
Investigate the development of a dance style across different historical and social contexts — analyse how social and environmental factors shaped the evolution of the style
elaborations: analysing dances from a range of times and locations, considering how a single realistic movement can be manipulated from representational to symbolic
investigating the development of dance styles in different artistic, social, environmental, historical or cultural contexts
using Viewpoints to explore questions about choreographic intention and ideas expressed
comparing use of elements of dance and choreographic devices across genres, cultures, times and places
investigating how digital tools and immersive technologies such as VR are influencing choreography and performance

AC9ADA8E02.minimum_width: Identify at least one example of First Nations Australian dance and explain what makes it culturally significant; describe what respectful engagement with First Nations dance looks like in practice.
AC9ADA8E02.typical_width: Investigate the diversity of First Nations Australian dance with attention to ICIP rights and protocols; analyse specific examples and explain how respectful and culturally responsive approaches apply in dance practice.
wider: Investigate a specific case of cultural appropriation in dance where ICIP rights were denied — explain what happened, who was harmed, and what a respectful alternative would have looked like
Use a map of First Nations Australian language groups to identify where choreographers and performers are working — investigate the geographic and cultural diversity of First Nations dance practice
Analyse how linear and non-linear narrative is used in specific First Nations Australian dance works to explore issues of identity, relationships or empathy
elaborations: exploring information about ICIP rights to help dance practitioners make ethical choices
using and annotating a map of First Nations Australian language groups to identify where First Nations choreographers and performers are working
analysing how linear and non-linear narrative is used in specific First Nations Australian dance works
investigating cultural appropriation examples where ICIP rights have been denied and how situations could have been approached respectfully

AC9ADA8P01.minimum_width: Rehearse and perform a dance for an audience using at least one technical and one expressive skill deliberately; introduce the dance to the audience with basic contextual information.
AC9ADA8P01.typical_width: Rehearse and perform dance using technical and expressive skills that serve the choreographic intent; use production elements and audience introduction strategies to communicate key ideas; evaluate performance outcomes.
wider: Use production elements (projection, soundscape, special effects) to extend communication of the dance's creative intention beyond the movement alone — evaluate how production choices change the audience experience
Develop and use specific rehearsal strategies (spotting, spatial planning, video review) to enhance confidence, clarity and musicality in performance
Create a program note or voice-over introduction using style-specific dance terminology that communicates choreographic intent to an unfamiliar audience
elaborations: planning effective use of available performance spaces during rehearsals
using production elements such as projection, soundscape, music, special effects or voice-overs to share key ideas about creative intention
using technical and expressive skills and style-specific techniques when performing dance they have learnt and/or choreographed
using rehearsal strategies such as spotting to enhance confidence, clarity of movement, projection, focus and musicality
introducing their dance to an audience in a program note or voice-over using descriptive style-specific dance terminology
